key_insight: The variable-length Key-Value (KV) scene representation causes quadratic growth in compute/memory with image count; VGG-T^3 distills that KV space into a fixed-size MLP via test-time training, enabling constant-size offline feed-forward 3D reconstruction.
problem_solved: Removes the quadratic computation and memory bottleneck of offline feed-forward 3D reconstruction as the number of input images increases.
method: Extract a variable-length KV geometric representation from multi-view images.
Perform test-time training to distill the KV representation into a fixed-size Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) that encodes scene geometry.
Run offline feed-forward reconstruction using the compact MLP, making inference cost independent of image count.
impact: Allows practitioners to scale offline feed-forward 3D reconstruction to large image collections with drastically reduced memory and compute, making high-fidelity reconstructions more practical for mapping, AR/VR, and dataset creation.
visual_elements: Scaling chart: quadratic compute/memory (KV) vs constant compute/memory (fixed-size MLP)
Pipeline diagram: images → KV space → test-time distillation → fixed-size MLP → 3D output
Before/after visualizations: reconstructions from many images using original KV approach vs VGG-T^3
Resource infographic: bar icons comparing GPU memory and latency for KV vs distilled MLP
paper_title: VGG-T$^3$: Offline Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction at Scale
paper_authors: Sven Elflein, Ruilong Li, Sérgio Agostinho, Zan Gojcic, Laura Leal-Taixé
